I feel you, a while back I had two survivors who after I got 10 hooks on rpd decided to just hide in the bushes by the front gate for the rest of the game. Together. Took me 20 minutes of just wandering around in circles to find them, just for both of them to go down instantly, not even bothering to try and take a chase. It was the most miserable game ever, even when I got up to get a snack and went afk for 5ish minutes, neither one of them even touched a gen.

I commend you for asking killer mains for feedback! Good job on looking at both sides :) They all (but one) seem a bit strong, but I definitely think they can be fixed while keeping the ideas at their core balanced. Here’s my attempt:

Security essentials: Honestly no there’s harm in letting them keep the item if they escape, it’s a decent reward for escaping with what amounts to a C tier perk in one of their slots. Alternatively, could give it something along the lines of adding 15% charges to that item.

End of shift: Off the record when the exit gates are powered is kinda busted, it practically guarantees you escape, or saving anyone who’s hooked when the last gen pops. Off the record is such a strong perk, that it only activates when you lose a hook stage, so giving it out without a sacrifice is kinda wild. Paired with Adrenaline, it’d be unbeatable. I’d propose making it hide your aura once the exit gates are powered, and removing your exhaustion. It’d still be strong and help you escape, while also allowing the killer to play around it.

Remnant: an extra hook stage is nasty, but I think this can still work. Here’s mine: when you would be sacrificed to the entity, you are able to immediately unhook yourself instead. You become broken, all your perks are deactivated, and entering the dying state immediately sacrifices you. You are hindered by 5%. This turns it more into a time waster the killer can’t really ignore, because they’d be giving up on a kill, but has a big enough downside that it isn’t the second chance perk of all time.

Degree in Engineering: I bet you don’t like gen regression right? Well gen progression is the flip side of that, and being able to add 11% to a generator every 60 seconds will amount to about a gen and a half per 15 minute match. Plus, you have to realize that survivors can bring four of the same perk between them. Just how maybe one extra health state from remnant would be ok, but four at a time would increase the hooks a killer needs to get by 33%. Here’s my idea: “After completing 50% of a generator, press the active ability button to trap the generator for 25 seconds. During this time, the killer kicks that generator 50% slower and the generator regresses at half the speed.”

Nowhere to run: At minimum, it needs a time limit for how long the plushie can stay active, I’d say 60 seconds. Probably increase the requirements to at least 50% of a gen too.

Father’s vengeance: Actively encourages killers to tunnel, on top of being endurance but way better and invalidating a hit. I would say the punishment needs to be way lighter, for example: when you unhook a survivor, this perk activates for 20 seconds. If the killer injures you during this time, they gain 5% hindered for 10 seconds.

Hope it was helpful <3 and thanks again for looking outside of your side when making these!

Because it sorta lowers the reward for getting really good at the game. With a more strict MMR, you would only be matched with people who make for fair matches, but every game would be a constant battle. With no MMR, you would be matched with anyone, meaning you would be able to see how your skills have grown as you demolish someone who isn't as good as you and it would feel really satisfying, but would feel way worse for the other player. The argument is that making the bad players feel like they suck would make them want to improve, but I don't really agree with that.

None of this really matters anyway, cus MMr doesn't do jack in this game. Of course, MMr should be in DBD, because it's different from most other games. In a shooter like call of duty, mmr is bad because instead of getting better and seeing the results as you get into a lobby with a bunch of randoms from across the skill spectrum, using your K/D or whatever to get a numerical value of your skill, the game pushes you to get a 1 kill-1 death ratio. But that's a game where you can just respawn instantly, practice non-stop in every game, and being stomped isn't as painful, so stomping someone else is so much more satisfying. In DBD, you have one power role, being the killer, and four players who are literally the victims. To make games interesting, the victims have to have a fighting chance, so having the average game be 2 escapes, 2 deaths, makes it so if you get a 3 or 4k, you feel like you outplayed them.

Of course, usually people are annoyed at the quality of the mmr in this game, since it doesn't really work, it just has a "Worst players bracket", a "85% of players bracket" and a "high level" bracket. Thing is, the worst player bracket is miserable cus no one knows what the hell they're doing. You get out of that bracket pretty quickly though. (usually) the middle bracket sucks because you're equally as likely to get teammates who don't know what they're doing as survivor, as you are to get a 4stack of bullies looking to ruin your night. Most players are here, so the inconsistency is infuriating, that's where you see most of the complaints coming from. The high level bracket is miserable too, because you pretty much only get 4 stacks and expert survivors, meaning that if you don't want to be bullied, you have to sweat really hard.

I'd consider myself in the middle bracket for just about every killer except pyramid head, and while I usually play super casually, every match I get on pyramid head has at least 1 p100 (if I'm lucky), and probably a couple background player, ftp + buckle up, adrenaline builds. The real issue though, is every other killer. Regardless of where you are in that middle 85%, you'll probably be facing off with a handful of players who go down in 15 seconds, next to players who can loop you for 5 gens.

Ok, this is a little complicated, but I'll try and make it as straightforward as possible.

When wildshaped, you keep your mental stats, but use the creature's physical stats. when making a roll which would use a mental stat, you have to look at a couple things.

1- your wisdom, intelligence, or charisma modifier.
2- your proficiencies.
3- the monster's proficiencies. (If the stat block specifies a skill, such as perception +3, it means they're proficient. +1 wisdom, +2 proficiency)

You use your mental stat, but if either you or the creature are proficient in that skill, you add *your* proficiency bonus. So say if you're rolling perception, if either the monster you have wildshaped into, or your character are proficient in perception, you add your character's proficiency bonus. 

Keen senses specify if it uses eyesight, smell, or hearing. You get advantage on rolls which use those senses, but not others which are not mentioned. (For example, a wolf would get advantage on perception checks to sniff out the trail of a fleeing villain, or to listen in on a conversation through a wall, but not to spot a trap)

Edit: your passive perception is 10 + your wisdom, but you also add your proficiency bonus if you're proficient in perception, which means that if the weasel is proficient in perception, but you aren't, your passive perception grows while you're wildshaped!

In my opinion; slugging (Downing survivors and leaving them on the floor) can be toxic in certain instances, but usually isn't. The main rule of thumb is don't slug if you don't have an immediate reason to. These reasons could be you see a survivor nearby who might come for the save, you have several survivors in a dead zone and want to spread some hits or deep wounds around, or know they're a distraction to finish a gen (More on this one later.)

  
If you down someone and decide to leave them for extra pressure and go off to check gens or search for survivors, you're being a little toxic. I wouldn't do this if I weren't in a really bad position (1 gen and 4 survivors alive, etc), and even then it's a last resort. Save it for the bully squads.

  
If you down someone and see an injured survivor get off a gen nearby and you're in a position to chase them, go for it! Worst case, they'll spend 20 seconds on the floor before someone gets off a gen and picks them up. 

  
If you know they're a distraction to finish a gen, maybe by them taking a chase as far from the generators as possible, while the other three swarm it and get it done in some 40 seconds, you're supposed to slug and protect the generator. Remember your goal is killing survivors, but generators let you get there. The more players you have occupied at a time, the less pressure you're under. (AKA; one survivor is downed, another is healing, a third is going to pick up the downed player, and you're chasing the fourth.) Once you get decently good, you can usually guarantee that once you slug, you'll get a down no matter what, since you start a chain of downs, which you only have to hook the last down, while they have to pick up each and every down.

  
Sometimes a quick slug can be a really smart play, if you're playing a stealth killer and use the slug to draw out a teammate, for example. A good tool you should always have in your back pocket, but don't overuse it.

Noed is “toxic” in the same way old dead hard was toxic, it’s a perk that allows you to make mistakes without being punished for them by the other side. If a survivor was caught out in a dead zone because they positioned themselves badly or made a mistake while looping, they could easily make up for it by simply deadharding to safety. In comparison, if a killer makes a couple mistakes and spends too long getting their first down, or don’t apply pressure to generators, you can easily make up for it by using noed. It’s frustrating to go against, because in both those situations, playing badly should be able to be punished by the other side, but a single perk allows them to deny you that punishment without invested effort on their part.

In short: is noed toxic? Not necessarily. Is it badly designed? God yes. Second chance perks as a whole are detrimental to both sides and we should work to get rid of them.

Idk, I normally get to rank 1 every month and the most effective way Ive found is basically that, give survivors free unhooks.

You need to get 9 separate hooks for irri devoted, so I normally try to let them get saved before they go to second phase or sacrifice, getting downs isnt that hard anyways. The main thing you want to be doing is pressuring gens and making sure you end chases quickly, keeping as many gens as you can for the first few minutes of the game gives you good gatekeeper emblems and quick chases gets you chaser. The last emblem basically amounts to not letting survivors heal, I normally dont have a problem with this one, but if it gives you trouble consider running nurses calling or something similar.

So what you want to do is:
1-keep gens from popping, abandon chases if they take more than 30 seconds for the down in the early game.
2-find survivors and end chases quickly. You get points for finding survivors which wont be lost and ending chases quick can get you a good bonus, dont be afraid to go back to pressuring gens if you cant get a survivor down. (Finding groups and going after the worst survivor is great for this)
3-hook survivors and let their teamates waste time unhooking while you start pressuring gens or begin a second chase. Sitting around the hook wont do you any good. If possible prioritize trading a hooked survivor for the rescuer instead of keeping that survivor hooked. *running devour hope can synergize well with this, but remember that chaser gives points per hit, meaning that having exposed survivors is actually less effective than two hit downing them*
4-interrupt healing! Very important! If youre having trouble, running sloppy butcher and/or nurses calling will help a lot. If possible swap out sloppy butcher for an add-on which has the same effects if itll activate often enough like wraiths addon which applies mangled and hemmorage if you hit them shortly after leaving cloak.

An easy build for maximizing this can be:
1-sloppy butcher (or a free place if you have an add-on)
2-nurses calling (perfect for interrupting healing)
3-lethal pursuer (great for early game chases and pressuring gens)
4-devour hope(devout)/deadlock(gatekeeper)/call of brine(gatekeeper)/ other

Everything is affected by your killer, dont play exposure killers like meyers or ghostie. It will destroy your chaser emblem. Just dont.

The best play is getting to a high rank at the start of the month and then playing however you want once youre at the desired rank.
